# Tenma

> Tenma runs PHP 8.5 as a long-running process: one process runs the script once, then serves HTTP requests continuously from an event loop. In-memory state persists between requests. Every request runs in its own Fiber, and waiting (sleep, HTTP, Postgres, Redis, files) suspends only that fiber. It is asynchronous without `await`. Tenma is a single binary with PHP embedded. Its PHP API lives in the top-level namespaces `Http`, `Threading`, `FileSystem`, `Messaging`, `Data`, `Development` and `Lsp`; it is built in, not a Composer package.

Run a script with `tenma app.php`. A script that starts an `Http\Server` becomes a server; a script without one runs until no timers or ops are pending.

```php
use Http\{Request, Response};

// A bakery's product page with the week's forecast
new Http\Server(8080, function (Request $request) {
    $weather = new Http\Client()->get('https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=47.99&longitude=7.85&daily=temperature_2m_max');   // suspends this request only
    return Response::json(['path' => $request->path, 'weather' => $weather->json()]);
})->start();
```

Rules for writing code that runs under Tenma (fiber mode, `Http\Server`):

- A handler gets a `Http\Request` and returns a `Response`, `StreamedResponse`, `WebSocketResponse` or a string. Never use `$_GET`, `$_POST`, `$_COOKIE`, `$_SERVER`, `$_SESSION`, `header()` or `echo` for the response. Use `$request->query`, `form()`, `files()`, `cookies()`, `header()`, `json()`, `body`, `path`, `method`, `remoteAddress`, `host()`.
- Many requests run at the same time in one process. Statics, globals and singletons are shared by all of them, so never keep per-request state there. Use `Threading\AsyncLocal` for values that follow a request into its tasks, like the request ID.
- PHP's own network functions wait without blocking the worker: `fsockopen()`, `stream_socket_client()`, `file_get_contents('https://...')`, `stream_select()`, PDO with `mysql:` and `pgsql:` DSNs, mysqli, and every library on PHP's streams. What still blocks every request of the worker: curl, `socket_*()`, `sleep()`, `fopen()` and `file_get_contents()` on files, PDO SQLite. Use `Http\Client`, `FileSystem\FileInfo` and `Threading\Task::delay()` for those. `tenma --pdo-pgsql native` keeps libpq for Postgres (blocking).
- There is no `await` keyword. A call to an async function simply returns its result. Start work in parallel with `Threading\Task::all(a: fn () => ..., b: fn () => ...)`, which runs them concurrently and returns the results under the same keys, or with `Threading\Task::run(fn () => ...)`, which returns a `Task` with `await()` and `cancel()`.
- Waiting is only possible inside a request, a task or a timer. At the top level of the script, wrap it in `Threading\Task::run()`.
- A request's tasks and timers end with the request. If the client disconnects, the handler gets `Threading\Cancelled` where it waits, and its `finally` blocks run. Work that must finish regardless, like a payment, goes in `Threading\Task::detach()`.
- `exit()` inside a request ends only that request. `exit()` in the script, a timer or background work ends Tenma with that status.
- With `--workers N`, each worker has its own interpreter and memory. Shared state belongs in Postgres or Redis.
- Existing frameworks that rely on superglobals run unchanged with `new Http\ClassicServer(8080, fn () => $app->handleHttp())->start()`. There requests run one after another, with superglobals, `header()`, output and sessions as under FPM, and the async functions throw.

API at a glance:

- `Http\Server`: `new Server(port, handler, static: [...])->start()`; `Http\ClassicServer`: `new ClassicServer(port, app)->start()`.
- `Threading\Task`: `run(fn)`, `all(...fns)`, `detach(fn)` return or await tasks; `delay(seconds)` waits. `Threading\Timer`: `after(seconds, fn)`, `every(seconds, fn, overlap: false)` return a `Timer` with `cancel()`; `overlap: false` skips a tick while the previous call still runs. `Timer::loop(fn)` calls again after the seconds the call returns, `null` stops it: a sync that idles or backs off.
- `Threading\Durable`: `define(name, fn (string $key), version:)` at startup, `start(name, key)` runs the function once per key across every process; with `tenma --durable postgres://…` its journal lives in Postgres, so it survives crashes and restarts and goes on where it was. Inside it, `Threading\Signal::receive(name, timeout:)` waits for `Signal::send(name, payload)` from anywhere (also another process) and `Task::delay()` of a second or more waits in the database. Side effects outside ops run at least once.
- `Tenma\Plugin`: a shared library loaded with `tenma --plugin FILE` (or `plugins` in `tenma.json`), ABI in `tenma-plugin/tenma_plugin.h`: `call(plugin, function, bytes)` synchronous, `await(plugin, function, bytes)` the fiber waits, `adopt(plugin, $socket)` hands a WebSocket to the plugin, which writes to it from its own threads; the plugin posts events to `Messaging\Channel` subscriptions. `Process\Shutdown::register(fn)` runs when tenma stops, before the plugins shut down, bounded by `--stop-timeout`.
- `Messaging\Channel`: `new Channel(name)->publish(message)` reaches every `subscribe(fn (string $message))` on that channel in every worker, the sender's included. Messages are strings; `subscribe()` returns a `Subscription` with `cancel()` and ends with the request it was made in. With `tenma --pubsub redis://host`, or `Channel::connect(url)` at script startup for a Redis the script starts itself, messages go through Redis and reach every process.
- `Http\Client`: `new Client(timeout: 30)` with `get(url, headers)`, `post(url, body, headers)` and `send(method, url, headers, body)`, each returning a `ClientResponse` with `status`, `body`, `header()` and `json()`.
- `Development\Debugger::break()` stops at that line when an editor is connected through `--inspect`. `Development\Problems::report(source, list)` reports problems (`file`, `line`, `message`, optional `severity`, `column`) to the editor through `tenma lsp`, only under `--watch`; a call replaces the source's list. `Development\Watch::reloadedBy()` is the file whose change made `--watch` run the script again, null on the first run.
- `Data\Postgres`: `connect(url)`, `query()`, `first()`, `execute()`, `transaction(fn)`, with `$1`-style parameters; a PHP list for an array parameter (`$1::text[]`) goes as a Postgres array. `query($sql, $params, as: Row::of(...))` and `first(..., as:)` map each row. Connections are pooled per worker.
- `Data\Migrations`: `new Migrations($db)->apply(['001_users' => 'CREATE TABLE ...', '002_x' => fn (Postgres $tx) => ..., ...Migrations::files($dir)])` applies each step once, in order, all pending in one transaction under an advisory lock; returns the names applied.
- `Data\Redis`: `connect(url)`, `command(name, ...args)`, `get()`, `set(key, value, seconds)`.
- `FileSystem\FileInfo`: `exists()`, `read()`, `write()`, `append()`, `size()`, `modified()`, `copyTo()`, `moveTo()`, `delete()`; `FileSystem\DirectoryInfo`: `exists()`, `create(recursive:)`, `files(pattern)`, `directories()`, `moveTo()`, `delete(recursive:)`. Both hold a path, do no I/O until a method runs, and throw `RuntimeException` with errno as the code.
- `Http\Response`:
  - `json()`, `html()`, `redirect()`, then chain `->header(name, value, append:)` and `->cookie(...)`.
  - `stream(fn (Stream $out))` and `events(fn (EventStream $events))` for streaming and server-sent events.
  - `websocket(fn (WebSocket $socket))` for WebSockets: `receive()` returns null once the client is gone, `send()` writes and waits while the client is behind. A write to a closed connection throws `ConnectionClosed`.
- `hooks` in `tenma.json`: build steps (commands or PHP files returning a callable) for `tenma --watch` and `tenma build`, such as Tailwind or caches.
- `Lsp\Provider`: what a package adds to `tenma lsp`, the language server that runs next to the editor's PHP server. It names the class `$this` is bound to in a non-class file (tenma then completes `$this->` by reflection, and types loop variables and variables assigned in the file) and adds completions, definitions and diagnostics; `Lsp\Tokens` next to it adds semantic tokens (colours). `Lsp\Imports` next to it names the imports a file sees (`imports($file, $text)`: alias => class, the namespace under `''`); the file's own `use` statements and namespace win, and tenma then completes `Name::` and leads F12 and hover on class names. `Lsp\Variables` next to it types variables other than `$this` (`variables($file, $text)`: name without `$` => class), completed and followed like `$this`; the file's own assignments and loops win below them. `Lsp\Elements` next to it names element classes of array members (`elements($class)`: property name or `method()` => class) for loop typing, asked of every provider for every class; a member's own PHPDoc wins. A package names it in `composer.json` under `extra.tenma.lsp`.

CLI: `tenma app.php`, `--watch`, `--inspect` (a DAP debugger on 127.0.0.1:9229), `--workers N|auto`, `--max-body 10m`, `--max-requests N`, `--db-pool N`, `--pdo-pgsql native`, `--durable postgres://URL`, `--plugin FILE`, `--config tenma.json` (every option as JSON next to the script), `--stop-timeout 10`, `--request-timeout 30`, `--max-connections 1024`, `--tls-cert FILE --tls-key FILE` (HTTPS with HTTP/2 on every port, or only on `--tls-port N`; `kill -HUP` reloads the certificate), `-d name=value`, `-c php.ini`, `--stubs`, `--record DIR` (with `--record-on error`, `--record-max-size 50m`, `--record-max-body`, `--record-redact`), `tenma build`, `tenma lsp`, `tenma docs` and `tenma replay FILE [--until N | --request N] [--check]`, which plays a recorded journal into a fresh interpreter without I/O and, with `--inspect`, lets the debugger step back; `--request N` plays the startup part and one request alone, `tenma replay FILE --list` numbers the requests.

`tenma docs [<path>...] [--out <dir>]` writes Markdown reference pages (default `docs/reference`): one page per class, interface, trait and enum declared in the given PHP files or directories, at `<out>/<Namespace path>/<ShortName>.md`, plus an `index.md` per namespace folder that also documents the namespace's functions under `## Functions` (one `### name()` section each). It loads the code through the nearest `vendor/autoload.php` and reads signatures by reflection and prose from docblocks (`@param`, `@return`, `@throws`, `@template`, `@var`). Only public API is documented (protected too in classes that can be extended); `@internal` types and members are skipped. Pages have YAML front matter with `generated: true`; a run is deterministic, removes generated pages whose type is gone and never overwrites a page without that flag. Without paths it documents Tenma's own API.

## Docs

- [Documentation](https://github.com/tenma-runtime/tenma/blob/main/docs/index.md): install, a first app, and how the docs are organised
- [Guides](https://github.com/tenma-runtime/tenma/blob/main/docs/guides/index.md): concepts (process and workers, event loop and fibers, plain PHP under tenma, lifetime of a request, state, fiber and classic mode), one page per API (HTTP server, HTTP client, tasks and timers, streams, WebSockets, file system, Postgres, Redis and pub/sub, durable functions, native plugins), tooling (command line, watch mode, debugger, language server, diagnostics, record and replay, `tenma docs`) and operations (configuration, deployment)
- [Reference](https://github.com/tenma-runtime/tenma/blob/main/docs/reference/index.md): every class and method of the PHP API, generated by `tenma docs`
- [README](https://github.com/tenma-runtime/tenma/blob/main/README.md): install, the command line options and the development commands
- [PHP API stubs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tenma-runtime/stubs/main/tenma.php): every class, method and parameter with its docblock. This is the exact API; `tenma --stubs` prints it for the installed binary

## Packages

- [tenma/stubs](https://github.com/tenma-runtime/stubs): the stubs for IDEs and PHPStan, installed with `composer require --dev tenma/stubs`. They are never autoloaded
- [tenma/psr](https://github.com/tenma-runtime/psr): runs any PSR-15 app under Tenma with `new Http\Server(3000, Tenma\Psr\Psr::handler($app, new Psr17Factory()))->start()`. WebSockets and streams go out through `Tenma\Psr\Upgrade`
- [Io](https://github.com/io-framework/framework): a PHP framework that is itself a Tenma handler, with `new Http\Server(8080, $app)->start()`, and that hands requests over to WebSockets and streams with `Response::upgrade()`
- [Io Live](https://github.com/io-framework/live): live components for Io: state stays on the server, events and updates travel over one WebSocket, running under Tenma
- [Io Bakery](https://github.com/io-framework/bakery): the example app the docs quote, a bakery's shop with `Threading\Task::all()` on the product page, timers that keep web service answers in worker memory, an order board across workers through `Messaging\Channel::publish()`, and Postgres migrations as `tenma index.php db:migrate`

## Optional

- [Architecture](https://github.com/tenma-runtime/tenma/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md#files): Rust (tokio, hyper), the C shim that embeds PHP, the PHP standard library, and how fibers and ops resume
- [Not yet](https://github.com/tenma-runtime/tenma/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md#not-yet): no TLS for Postgres, blocking name resolution, no handler timeout, and request bodies are fully buffered
